correctness.rationale: For the eight vertices, squared distances equal one of seven coordinate subset sums. Their order is fixed except for the comparison of the largest coordinate square with the sum of the other two. Each Rips stage is identified exactly as a graph, two tetrahedra joined by four bridges, the join of two four-cycle independence complexes, or a cross-polytope boundary. The integral cycle lattice of the cube graph is generated by its six square boundaries with one primitive relation; diagonal additions fill precisely the two corresponding square faces and cause the stated five one-dimensional bar deaths, while coordinate edges give the three zero-dimensional merge levels. This proves the formulas for all positive real side lengths and all fields, including ties. verify.py independently checked mod-two persistent boundary reductions and critical-stage Betti numbers for 364 integer squared-length triples (2564 stages), with VERIFY_OK. Finite checks are supporting evidence, not the proof. Higher-dimensional claims are confined to a single three-sphere stage.

value.rationale: This is a complete natural geometric filtration and field-independent barcode for every aspect ratio of a 3D rectangular box, a canonical family of point clouds. Unlike a fixed regular-cube computation, it detects a sharp Pythagorean crossing that swaps a five-circle intermediate stage for two contractible components, and explicitly tracks all degree-one and degree-three persistent features through this transition. It is a motivated exact classification, not a selected arbitrary finite instance or an algebraic restatement of the known regular cube.
